title: Senior backend engineer, Northwind Pay
notes: Senior Backend Engineer, Payments Platform team at Northwind Pay. Interviewer: Sarah, platform lead. Round 2: background + system design. Want to come across as someone who has run high-scale systems in production.
profile: Priya Sharma. Senior backend engineer, 6 years. Zepto (2022-now): built and own the recommendations platform in Go, Kafka and Redis; serves 40k requests/s; cut p99 latency from 180 ms to 95 ms by moving feature lookups to a Redis cluster with request coalescing; led a team of 4. Hardest problem there: Kafka consumer lag during flash sales, fixed with partition rebalancing and backpressure. Flipkart (2019-2022): search indexing pipeline in Java, Elasticsearch, reduced index rebuild from 6 hours to 40 minutes. IIT Roorkee, B.Tech CS 2019.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Hi! Can you hear me okay?

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Yes, I can hear you fine. Thanks for having me.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Great. So I'm Sarah, I lead the platform team here. Our team builds the payments infrastructure, and we handle about two million transactions a day.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: So, to start, could you walk me through your background and what you've been working on recently?

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Sure. I'm a backend engineer with about six years of experience. For the last three years I've been at Zepto, where I built and own the recommendations platform.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Nice. What was the hardest scaling problem you hit on that platform, and how did you fix it?

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: The hardest one was Kafka consumer lag during flash sales. We fixed it with partition rebalancing and backpressure on the producers.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Let's switch gears. How would you design a rate limiter for a public API that serves millions of users?

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Okay. I'd start with a token bucket per API key, with the counters stored in Redis.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: And how would that work across multiple data centers?

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Good question. I would keep local buckets in each region and sync them asynchronously.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Alright, that's all from my side. Do you have any questions for me?

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Yes, I do have a couple.
